T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(hour_of_day() < n_off | hour_of_day() >= n_on, -drop, drop - drop)
notebook.mechanism: Night setback: supply temperature is reduced during night hours, on top of PI control.
notebook.targets: hour-of-day residual pattern
notebook.refute: If the fitted drop is not positive, or if the hour-of-day residual does not improve, then the missing mechanism is not a night setback.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: only single <, >, <=, >= comparisons

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(hour_of_day() >= n_on & hour_of_day() < n_boost_end, boost, boost - boost)
notebook.mechanism: Morning recovery boost: supply temperature is increased for a few hours after night setback to bring room up to temperature.
notebook.targets: midday negative residual (actual higher than predicted)
notebook.refute: If the fitted boost is not positive, or if the midday residual does not improve, then the missing mechanism is not a morning recovery boost.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: only single <, >, <=, >= comparisons

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + slope * T_out
notebook.mechanism: Weather compensation added to PI control: supply temperature increases as outdoor temperature falls, on top of room feedback.
notebook.targets: cold outdoor band bias and correlation with outdoor
notebook.refute: If adding outdoor reset does not reduce the cold-band residual or if the fitted slope is near zero, then the missing mechanism is not weather compensation.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost)
notebook.mechanism: Weekend boost: supply temperature is increased on weekends, on top of PI control.
notebook.targets: weekend-minus-weekday difference
notebook.refute: If the fitted boost is not positive, or if the weekend residual does not improve, then the missing mechanism is not a weekend boost.

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where((hour_of_day() < n_off) | (hour_of_day() >= n_on), -drop, drop - drop)
notebook.mechanism: PID room-temperature control with a night setback: the setpoint is lowered by a fixed offset during the unoccupied window, so the controller asks for less supply water overnight and the room drifts slightly below the daytime setpoint. (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: night-time positive residual (00-06) and the hour-of-day wave in the residual report
notebook.refute: If the fitted n_on/n_off do not align with the observed hour-of-day residual wave, or if the drop parameter collapses to zero, the setback mechanism is not supported.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_boost_end), boost, boost - boost)
notebook.mechanism: PID control with an optimal-start morning boost: the controller raises the effective setpoint for a fixed window before occupancy to pull the room up to temperature, producing extra supply water in the early hours and a slight overshoot that decays later. (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: morning warm-up residual (positive hours 00-06, negative midday) and the recovery ramp after the unoccupied period
notebook.refute: If the boost window does not sit in the early morning, or if boost collapses to zero, the morning-boost mechanism is not supported.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) - ema(boost * (sp - T_room), tau)
notebook.mechanism: Weekend boost is applied but a slow first-order recovery/decay term (e.g. thermal mass of the fireplace mass cooling after weekend setback) subtracts a lagged fraction of the boost, producing a negative residual that grows through the day and is larger on weekends.
notebook.targets: weekend_minus_weekday = -0.057 and the afternoon negative residual trough (hours 12-17)
notebook.refute: If the fitted tau collapses to near-zero or the boost coefficient goes to zero, the weekend residual would not be explained by a lagged boost term.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + slope * (T_out - ema(T_out, ti))
notebook.mechanism: Controller uses a weather-compensation curve based on a filtered outdoor temperature rather than instantaneous T_out; the residual is the difference between the instantaneous and filtered outdoor signal times a slope, which is largest during cold snaps.
notebook.targets: mean_by_outdoor_band showing -0.20 at <0C and -0.15 at 0-5C, plus corr_with_outdoor = 0.098
notebook.refute: If the fitted slope is near zero or the filtered-vs-instantaneous difference does not correlate with the cold-band residuals, weather compensation on filtered T_out is not the mechanism.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + where(hour_of_day() < n_off, -boost, boost - boost)
notebook.mechanism: A night setback schedule: the controller drops the effective setpoint during early-morning hours, so the model (which assumes constant setpoint) over-predicts supply at night and under-predicts during the day when the controller catches up.
notebook.targets: the overnight positive residual (hours 0-6, +0.03) and the daytime negative trough (hours 12-17, -0.05)
notebook.refute: If the fitted n_off lands outside the 0-6 window or the boost coefficient is near zero, a night setback does not explain the diurnal residual shape.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + where(month() >= month_n, boost, boost - boost)
notebook.mechanism: Shoulder-season changeover: the controller switches between heating modes (or enables a seasonal boost) at a calendar month boundary, producing a step in supply temperature that the continuous model cannot capture.
notebook.targets: mean_by_month showing -0.14 in April and -0.16 in October vs near-zero in summer months
notebook.refute: If the fitted month_n falls in summer or the boost is near zero, a seasonal changeover does not explain the shoulder-month residuals.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + slope_ema * (T_out - ema(T_out, tau))
notebook.mechanism: Weather-compensated reset: the controller adds a term proportional to the deviation of outdoor temperature from its slow moving average, so a cold snap (T_out below its EMA) raises supply and a warm spell lowers it. This is a standard outdoor-reset curve with a filtered reference rather than the raw T_out used in M1.1/M2.2.
notebook.targets: mean_by_outdoor_band: negative residual at cold outdoor (<0, 0-5) and the corr_with_outdoor=0.098; also the diurnal residual trough at 14-16.
notebook.refute: If the fitted tau collapses to a very short or very long horizon and the term's coefficient goes to zero, or if held-out RMSE does not improve over M1.3, the residual's outdoor-band structure is not a filtered-outdoor reset effect.

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + where(hour_of_day() < n_off, -drop, drop - drop)
notebook.mechanism: Night setback with morning recovery: the controller lowers the supply setpoint during a night window (early hours) and lets the integral term recover it during the day. The residual's sign flip at ~08:00 is the recovery transient the pure proportional+integral loop cannot reproduce.
notebook.targets: mean_by_local_hour: positive residual 0-6 and negative residual 12-18; the night_00_06_weekday_minus_weekend=0.041.
notebook.refute: If the fitted n_off lands outside the 0-8 window, or if the term is not significant in held-out data, the diurnal residual is not a setback schedule but something else (e.g Calibration drift).

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + gain_h * (T_room - ema(T_room, tau))
notebook.mechanism: Adaptive/self-tuning room feedback: the controller adds a correction proportional to the recent room-temperature trend (room minus its own EMA), i.e. a derivative-like term on the room state. In shoulder months the room drifts more, so this term is larger, explaining the month-dependent residual.
notebook.targets: mean_by_month: April and October residuals (-0.139, -0.158) versus mid-summer near zero; also the weekend_minus_weekday=-0.057.
notebook.refute: If the fitted tau is outside a plausible derivative horizon (minutes to a couple of hours) or the term does not reduce the April/October bias in held-out data, the seasonal residual is not a room-derivative effect.

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + where(month() >= n_summer, -boost, boost - boost)
notebook.mechanism: Seasonal changeover / heating-lockout: the controller disables or reduces heating above a calendar threshold (summer mode), so shoulder months carry a systematic offset relative to the pure loop. This is distinct from M2.4, which added a positive boost in summer rather than a negative one in the shoulder months.
notebook.targets: mean_by_month: the strong negative residual in April and October and near-zero in June-August; the corr_with_humidity=0.231.
notebook.refute: If the fitted n_summer falls in a month where the residual is already near zero, or if the term does not improve held-out RMSE over M1.3, the month structure is not a calendar changeover.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + slope * (T_out - ema(T_out, ti))
notebook.mechanism: weather-compensated reset with a slow outdoor filter: the controller tracks filtered outdoor temperature rather than instantaneous outdoor temperature, so the supply offset lags weather swings and leaves a diurnal residual pattern (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: weekend_minus_weekday and corr_with_outdoor; the hour-of-day residual arc that the plain outdoor term cannot follow
notebook.refute: held-out RMSE no better than M1.3, or the fitted slope collapsing to zero, or the ema time constant hitting its bound
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + where(hour_of_day() < n_off, -boost, boost - boost)
notebook.mechanism: night setback: the controller lowers the supply setpoint during the early-morning hours, so the model over-predicts heat then and the residual is positive before dawn (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: night_00_06_weekday_minus_weekend and the positive early-morning residual band in mean_by_local_hour
notebook.refute: held-out RMSE no better than M1.3, or the fitted n_off landing outside the night window, or the boost sign flipping to a morning boost
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where(weekday() >= n_weekend, boost, boost - boost) + gain * (T_room - ema(T_room, ti))
notebook.mechanism: room-temperature feedback trim: the controller adds a term proportional to how fast room temperature is drifting from its own filtered value, correcting overshoot that the pure proportional-plus-integral law misses (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: the midday negative residual trough in mean_by_local_hour and the weekend_minus_weekday offset
notebook.refute: held-out RMSE no better than M1.3, or the fitted gain indistinguishable from zero, or the term worsening the midday residual instead of flattening it
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)
stop: 2 rounds without a program improving the held-out score by more than the noise band

notebook.expr: level + slope * T_out - midday_drop * (hour_of_day() >= midday_start & hour_of_day() < midday_end)
notebook.mechanism: Controller reduces supply temperature during peak solar/occupancy hours to avoid overheating, a solar compensation or day setback.
notebook.targets: mean_by_local_hour negative midday residual
notebook.refute: If fitted midday_drop is not significantly negative or the held-out error does not improve, the midday residual is not explained by a scheduled supply reduction.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: only single <, >, <=, >= comparisons

notebook.expr: level + slope * T_out + season_offset * (month() >= season_start & month() <= season_end)
notebook.mechanism: Calendar-based seasonal changeover or shoulder-season reset: a month window applies a fixed supply temperature offset.
notebook.targets: mean_by_month May negative and September/October positive residual
notebook.refute: If season_offset is not significant or the fitted month window does not cover the anomalous months, the monthly residual is not a calendar offset.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: only single <, >, <=, >= comparisons

notebook.expr: where(hour_of_day() >= midday_start & hour_of_day() < midday_end, level + slope * T_out - midday_drop, level + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: a scheduled midday setback / reduced-flow window in the controller's daily program: during a fixed block of local clock hours the supply setpoint is shifted down by a fixed offset, while the rest of the day follows the outdoor-reset curve (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: the broad negative residual trough in mean_by_local_hour between late morning and late afternoon, where the plain weather-compensation curve over-predicts supply temperature
notebook.refute: the fitter collapses the window (start equal to end, or a window covering nearly all or none of the day) or drives the offset to zero, or held-out RMSE does not beat the plain reset curve S1; also refuted if the fitted window does not overlap the hours where the residual is most negative
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: only single <, >, <=, >= comparisons

notebook.expr: where(month() >= season_start & month() <= season_end, level + slope * T_out + season_offset, level + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: a seasonal changeover / calendar-based offset in the controller, e.g. a summer-winter mode switch or a seasonal reset-curve shift that adds a fixed bias to the supply setpoint for a contiguous block of months (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: the month-blocked residual structure: a large negative residual in the late-spring month and positive residuals in the early-autumn months, which a single outdoor-reset line cannot absorb
notebook.refute: the fitted month block is empty or spans the whole year, or the offset is negligible, or the improvement disappears on held-out months; also refuted if the residual month pattern is better explained by an outdoor-temperature or humidity term rather than by calendar month
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: only single <, >, <=, >= comparisons

notebook.expr: level + slope * T_out + boost * max(cutoff - T_out, T_out - T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Low outdoor temperature boost: the outdoor reset curve becomes steeper below a cutoff, increasing supply to protect against cold.

notebook.targets: weekday/weekend night difference and overall weekend negative residual
notebook.refute: if the fitted weekend night drop is negligible or the weekday/weekend night residual does not shrink, the weekend-night difference is not a deeper setback
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where(hour_of_day() < n_morning, level + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room) + boost_morning, level + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room))
notebook.mechanism: weather-compensated supply with proportional room feedback, plus a morning warm-up boost before the early cutoff hour (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: morning positive residual bump (hours 4-8) on top of the room-feedback term
notebook.refute: if the fitted n_morning lands outside the early-morning window, or boost_morning fits to zero, or held-out RMSE does not improve over M1.4
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)
stop: 2 rounds without a program improving the held-out score by more than the noise band
